legend: ICPC Square is a hotel provided by the ICPC Committee for the accommodation of the participants. It consists of N%%ZSMJ0%% floors (numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to N%%ZSMJ2%%). This hotel has a very unique elevator. If a person is currently at floor x%%ZSMJ3%%, by riding the elevator once, they can go to floor y%%ZSMJ4%% if and only if y%%ZSMJ5%% is a multiple of x%%ZSMJ6%% and y−x≤D%%ZSMJ7%%.
You are currently at floor S%%ZSMJ8%%. You want to go to the highest possible floor by riding the elevator zero or more times. Determine the highest floor you can reach.
input: A single line consisting of three integers N%%ZSMJ9%% D%%ZSMJ10%% S%%ZSMJ11%% (2≤N≤1012;1≤D≤N−1;1≤S≤N%%ZSMJ12%%).
output: Output a single integer representing the highest floor you can reach by riding the elevator zero or more times.
note: First, ride the elevator from floor 3%%ZSMJ13%% to floor 15%%ZSMJ14%%. This is possible because 15%%ZSMJ15%% is a multiple of 3%%ZSMJ16%% and 15−3≤35%%ZSMJ17%%. Then, ride the elevator from floor 15%%ZSMJ18%% to floor 30%%ZSMJ19%%. This is possible because 30%%ZSMJ20%% is a multiple of 15%%ZSMJ21%% and 30−15≤35%%ZSMJ22%%. Finally, ride the elevator from floor 30%%ZSMJ23%% to floor 60%%ZSMJ24%%. This is possible because 60%%ZSMJ25%% is a multiple of 30%%ZSMJ26%% and 60−30≤35%%ZSMJ27%%.
